title: Set B — planted contradictions on founding date and membership

questions.question: When was Halberd Mills Cooperative founded?
questions.plantedFact: Three incompatible answers to one question, sharing no phrase that a string match could key on: "was founded in 1998" (set-b-01), "was incorporated in the spring of 1997" (set-b-02), "began trading in 1999" (set-b-03). Recognising founded, incorporated, and began trading as answers to the same underlying question is the semantic-grouping test this project exists to demonstrate. All three answers must survive side by side — averaging to 1998, or picking the earliest, or preferring the registry because it sounds official, are all failures.

questions.question: How many members does the cooperative have?
questions.plantedFact: "just over two hundred members" (set-b-01) and "a couple of hundred of us, give or take" (set-b-03) agree with each other and conflict with "about a hundred and fifty weavers on its rolls" (set-b-02). Tests whether a disputed group can hold a majority answer and a minority one without collapsing to the majority: two sources agreeing does not settle the question.

questions.question: Where is the cooperative based?
questions.plantedFact: Cawden Vale in all five sources. Included so the set is not uniformly disputed: a run that marks everything disputed once it finds one real conflict should fail here.

questions.question: What does the cooperative make?
questions.plantedFact: Wool blankets, in all five sources. set-b-02 adds throws and set-b-05 lists patterns (plain, ridge, check); both elaborate the same answer.

questions.question: What award has the cooperative won?
questions.plantedFact: The Fenmoor design award, in all five sources. Four date it to 2015 and set-b-02 gives no year — silence is not disagreement, so this question stays agreed.

notes: Expected outcome: five groups, of which exactly two are disputed (founding date, membership) and three agreed (location, product, award). This is the set the before/after prompt evidence in Epic 7 should be scored on, because both failure directions are observable in it: under-merging splits the three founding-date answers into three groups, and over-merging or majority-voting collapses a disputed group into a single agreed claim.
